# onetsolutions_domain_settings (Resource)

Manages the name servers, automatic renewal, registry lock and WHOIS privacy of a registered domain.

The domain must already be registered in the project, in the console or with
`onetsolutions_domain`. A setting left unset is not managed and
reports the domain's current value.

-> **Destroying only removes it from the state.** This resource never orders, transfers, renews or
deletes a domain. Destroying it **only removes it from the Terraform state**: the domain stays
registered and keeps its name servers, automatic renewal, lock and WHOIS privacy exactly as they
are. With `auto_renew = true` the domain keeps renewing, and being billed, after the resource is
destroyed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

resource "onetsolutions_dns_zone" "example" {
  zone_name = "example.com"
}

# Delegate the domain to its zone, keep it locked, hide the registrant from WHOIS.
resource "onetsolutions_domain_settings" "example" {
  domain_id     = data.onetsolutions_domain.example.id
  nameservers   = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.nameservers
  auto_renew    = true
  locked        = true
  whois_privacy = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (String) The UUID of the domain (see `onetsolutions_domain`). Changing it moves the resource to another domain (the previous domain is left unchanged).

### Optional

- `auto_renew` (Boolean) Whether the domain renews automatically before it expires.
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the domain is locked at the registry against transfers.
- `nameservers` (List of String) The name servers the domain is delegated to, 2 to 5, in order, lowercase without a trailing dot — for instance the `nameservers` of an `onetsolutions_dns_zone`.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `whois_privacy` (Boolean) Whether the registrant's contact details are hidden from WHOIS.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The UUID of the domain.
- `name` (String) The domain name.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `15m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `15m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_domain_settings.example
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/7d6c5b4a-3f2e-4d1c-9b8a-7f6e5d4c3b2a"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<domain_id>, or <domain_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_domain_settings.example 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/7d6c5b4a-3f2e-4d1c-9b8a-7f6e5d4c3b2a
```
